title: Mildred Major and Emma Zeno Interview, 1969-03-28

blocks.x: All right, today is March 28, 1969, and I'm interviewing Mildred Major and also her mother, Alice. Emma. Emma. Yeah. And all right, Mildred, what are your earliest memories of at home and where were you living and, you know, what can you remember at that time?
Well, I can remember very little, like I told you, Mandeville was the first place that I knew we lived. Yeah. I was rather small then.
Yeah.

You actually confirmed my grandfather this morning. I don't remember him too well. I remember him like a shadow, a small house. I was just a kid. Mm-hmm. Very little. And the next memories I have with my father was Regalige. And all I can remember then is water and a crane.
What was this, did you say?
Regalige. Remember his liege was. Regalige.
Regalige. Regalige.
Regalige. He was with the, uh, camp camp. Uh, camp, huh?
Yeah.
You know, small, real small then. And all I can remember is water and a crane. That's all I can remember. You know, cranes to come every day.
And this is at Mandeville you're talking about?
No, this is in Regalige. Regalige.
Regalige. Regalige. Where the palace is that?
It's over on the Mandeville.
Oh, it's close to now. It's close to Mandeville. Yeah.

Now, in, uh, here in the city, New Orleans, I remember living on St. Claude Street. St. Claude between Espanade and Calarick. That's where I can remember my dad coming from there. Yes. Well, he taught me how to sew. She drew for me a picture on a piece of rag and I learned how to embroider on that.
Yeah.
My father used to take me, when he learned small town play music, used to take me on picnets with him. And he learned, he tried to learn me how to cook, but I never learned from him.
Yeah.
I do have a nice time when my daddy was home, but it wasn't too much of a life that my daddy smoked. And he left us rather early. That's not real. Yes. That's about all I can remember was my father.
Do you remember going on picnics to yourself? Oh, yeah.

He used to take me on picnics with him. And that was another time he tried to make me interested in his music. They were at the Oratorium Square here on Sinan and St. Claude. We had a pop concert. And I sang at the concert. Very nice it was. Had a nice write-up in the items, paper files.
How old were you then?
I must have been around 18 years old. About 18. And you sang at the concert? Yeah. Mr. Nick, I don't know if you remember his manager. I used to manage him. I remember Nick.
Oh, Nick. Oh, Gagliana.
Well, he was with my father then at that time.
Oh, yes. That would have been in the, that would have been maybe in the early 50s or late 40s.

Oh, dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear

segments.title: Opening and earliest memory of Mandeville
segments.summary: Interviewer opens the March 28, 1969 session with Mildred Major and her mother; Mildred recalls Mandeville as her first home.

segments.title: Memories of her grandfather and the camp near Mandeville
segments.summary: She remembers her grandfather like a shadow, then a place near Mandeville where her father was at a camp, recalling only water and a crane.

segments.title: Life on St. Claude Street and her father
segments.summary: In New Orleans she lived on St. Claude; her father taught her to embroider, took her on picnics and tried to teach cooking, but left the family early.

segments.title: Singing at a pop concert with her father's band and Nick
segments.summary: Picnics led to her singing at a pop concert at the Square at about age 18, with Nick, her father's manager; the end of the transcript degenerates into garbled repetition.
